close_reason: Primary concerns (i64→usize, u64→usize) addressed by JMAP-qz9v.48 / .47. Remaining usize→u64 casts are lossless and match canonical mail-server pattern.
description:
Site: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/memory.rs:596-618 (MemoryBackend::query_objects). Same shape recurs in query_changes (line 625+).

Current code:

    let total = ids.len() as u64;                                  // L596
    let start = if position >= 0 {
        (position as usize).min(ids.len())                         // L604: i64 -> usize
    } else {
        let neg = position.saturating_neg() as usize;              // L606: i64 -> usize
        ids.len().saturating_sub(neg)
    };
    ids = ids[start..]
        .iter()
        .take(limit.map_or(usize::MAX, |n| n as usize))            // L612: u64 -> usize
        .cloned()
        .collect();
    Ok(QueryResult::new(ids, start as i64, ...))                   // L618: usize -> i64

Five 'as' casts across a 25-line span, each one a different signed/unsigned boundary:
- L596 usize -> u64: lossless on 32-bit, lossless on 64-bit (usize is always <= u64); safe in practice but as-cast loses the intent.
- L604 i64 -> usize: on 32-bit pointers, an i64 position of 2^33 silently truncates to a small usize. position was already validated as >= 0 above so the sign-cast is fine, but the truncation isn't.
- L606 i64 -> usize: after saturating_neg(), value is in [0, i64::MAX]; on 32-bit pointers same truncation problem.
- L612 u64 -> usize: limit comes off the wire as u64; on 32-bit a wire-supplied limit of 2^33 silently becomes a small number.
- L618 usize -> i64: lossless on 32-bit, lossless-ish on 64-bit (usize > i64::MAX is the underflow boundary but ids.len() is bounded by available memory). Acceptable but not idiomatic.

What idiomatic Rust does: use usize::try_from(i64_val).unwrap_or(usize::MAX) for the i64 -> usize conversions (this gives saturating behavior at the platform-pointer-size boundary instead of silent truncation). For usize -> i64, i64::try_from(usize_val).expect('len fits in i64 — total memory < 8 EiB') with a load-bearing comment. The pattern across the file should be that any size_t-style crossing uses try_from explicitly.

What goes wrong if left: on 64-bit hosts (the workspace's only test target today), nothing — every value fits. On 32-bit (not a current target but the kit's downstream-consumer story explicitly says 'consumers bring everything', so consumers might build for 32-bit Linux / wasm32 / embedded), a malicious or buggy client that sends a multi-gigabyte position or limit gets silently truncated to a small number, which is the kind of off-by-orders-of-magnitude bug that produces spec-incorrect results without panic. The reference impl shouldn't model this casual approach to numeric boundaries for downstream copy-paste.

This is a clippy::pedantic finding (cast_possible_truncation, cast_sign_loss, cast_possible_wrap fire on every site) that the previous rusty pass flagged as a confidence gap: 'cargo clippy --workspace -- -W clippy::pedantic was run against this diff to surface lints I'd miss by eyeball.' This pass ran it and these are the highest-signal hits in chat-server scope.
title: memory.rs query_objects: i64/u64/usize as-casts on position/limit are non-idiomatic and lossy on 32-bit targets
